title: Flat degree-zero tensor commutes with cohomology on a ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the universe of module sheaves, and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings. Use the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its unbounded derived category $Q:\operatorname{CoCh}(R)\to D(R)$ and cohomology functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], ordinary sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Give $D(R)$ the K-flat derived tensor and its canonical localization comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Let $L$ be a flat $R$-module sheaf, meaning $F_L=(-)\otimes_R L$ is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and write $L[0]$ for its degree-zero complex or its image under $Q$. Then $L[0]$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] and has flat terms. For every unbounded cochain complex $C$, the canonical degreewise identification of $\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_R L[0])$ with $(C^n\otimes_R L,d_C^n\otimes1_L)_n$ induces isomorphisms
$$c^i_{C,L}:H^i(\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_R L[0]))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(C)\otimes_R L.$$
They are induced by the exact tensor identifications of cycles and boundaries, and are natural in cochain maps $C\to C'$ and arbitrary module maps $L\to L'$ between flat sheaves. For every $K\in D(R)$ there are isomorphisms
$$\gamma^i_{K,L}:\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^i(K)\otimes_R L\qquad(i\in\mathbf Z),$$
natural simultaneously in $K$ and maps between flat $L$. Their normalization is as follows: if $K=QC$ and $p:P\to C$ is any flat-term K-flat resolution, $\gamma^i_{QC,L}$ is, under the canonical derived-tensor model comparison, the composite of $c^i_{P,L}$ and $H^i(p)\otimes1_L$. It is independent of the resolution. No boundedness, constructibility or Tor-amplitude hypothesis on $K$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor and preceding localization construction, flat degree-zero specialization; the cycle-quotient comparison and its simultaneous naturality are the agent-extracted arguments of lem-fd-flat-constructible-tensor, returned proof steps 1-2.

proof.text: Use the already proved flat-single derived normalization theorem to obtain K-flatness and flat terms of L[0]. Transfer exactness of the defining site tensor to tensorRight L by siteSheafTensorRightIso. The existing mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso identifies total tensor with termwise tensor. Compose its image under homology with ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso to define c. ShortComplex.mapCyclesIso and the left homology data quotient equation give exactly the two cycle equations.

Check naturality of mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso on each direct-sum summand. If the second degree is nonzero its source is zero. On (i,0), functoriality and naturality of the single degree-zero identification give the desired square for f and g. Apply homology. ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso_hom_naturality handles f, and ShortComplex.homologyMap_mapNatTrans handles the natural transformation tensorRight L to tensorRight L' given by g. Their composition is simultaneous cochain naturality of c.

Apply fixed-K-flat tensor triangulated descent to L[0] and invert its right comparison to obtain a with the stated representativeIso normalization. For g compare the two natural transformations on K-flat flat-term complexes P: the left fixed-factor comparison for P is natural in L[0], so its inverse gives equality there. For arbitrary K choose a K-flat flat-term quasi-isomorphism P to K. Naturality and cancellation of the invertible image of that quasi-isomorphism extend equality to K.

Apply derived cohomology to a, then the cohomology factorization isomorphism and c, and finally inverse tensor of the source cohomology factorization. This is a natural isomorphism after restriction along Q. Extend it using Localization.liftNatIso to define gamma. The lift value on QK and cancellation give the displayed representative equation. Naturality in g follows after restriction along Q from the a and c squares; Localization.natTrans_ext extends it to every derived object.

Apply naturality of gamma to Qp. Replace representativeIso.hom by a.inv on P using normalization, and use the representative equation for gamma at P to cancel a.hom with a.inv. Naturality of homologyFunctorFactors.inv for p gives the final formula. This holds for every specified resolution p, proving independence without a map between resolutions.

The item is not on the side-live route-pivot drop list and is still unsplit live, so nothing supersedes it. It has no repair note and no new nodes, and no SGA source is used. Step 1: in degree n only the (n,0) summand of Tot(C⊗L[0]) is nonzero, and the differential reduces to d_C⊗1 because d_{L[0]}=0; this holds for unbounded C. Step 2: L flat means F_L is exact, and the exact-functor leaf gives c^i together with the cycle and boundary compatibilities. Step 3: I checked the naturality in an arbitrary u:L→L' term by term. Cancelling the cycle inclusion (a mono) gives Z(τ)k_L=k_{L'}τ_Z, and then cancelling the epi q_L k_L gives the naturality square; no assumption on u is needed. Step 4: L[0] is K-flat with flat terms. Here A⊗L[0] puts L[0] on the right, matching the K-flat definition, and 0 is flat. Step 5: the right-factor form of lem-trf-site-one-sided-tensor-normalization gives a natural in C and in maps of the fixed factor. Localization (2) lifts b and its inverse, and (3) makes the u-square commute on all of D(R). Step 6: a_P=δ^{-1} because P and L[0] lie in P_R, so m=(Qp⊗1)δ is exactly the item's model comparison. Then γH^i(m)=(H^i p⊗1)c_P, which also gives independence of the resolution. Edge cases checked: L=0, L=R, acyclic C, C unbounded in both directions, u=0, and the nonflat R=Z, L=Z/2 (flatness is a hypothesis and is never dropped). Accepted tool uses: lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed, lem-pc-kflat-resolution and lem-trf-site-one-sided-tensor-normalization.
